newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador January exports rise, deficit narrows.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador January exports rise, deficit narrows.

text.p: El Salvador's exports rose to $211 million in January, a 33 percent increase from the same month of 1996, the Central Reserve Bank said on Monday.
El Salvador imported $268 million worth of goods in the most recent period, narrowing its monthly trade deficit to $57 million from $94 million in January 1996.
El Salvador exported $158 million worth of goods and imported $252 million in the first month of 1996.
Of the total exports in January 1997, $78 million came from coffee and sugar and an equal amount from textiles.
Some $41 million of exports went to other Central American countries, $31 million to the United States and $17 million to Europe.
Leading imports were petroleum, fertilizers and non-durable consumer goods, according to the report, which did not provide specific figures.
